AI Meeting Assistant
That Works Across Your Meetings

Meetily records each call on your own computer, writes up the decisions and action items, and keeps a history you can search. With Pro, Claude, Codex, Cursor or Windsurf can look through past meetings and answer questions about them.
More Than Notes From One Call
Notes are the starting point. Meetily also keeps track of what was said across meetings and hands it to the tools you use. See how speaker diarization and the Meetily MCP server work.
Each summary pulls out what was decided and what needs doing, so nobody rebuilds the follow-up list from memory.
Shape the write-up for a standup, a client call or a 1:1. Pro ships 6 built-in templates and lets you write your own.
Search and replace across transcripts and summaries in the app. In Pro, the meetily-pro CLI searches every transcript from a script.
Pro labels each speaker on your device, live or on imported audio. Rename a speaker once and the whole transcript follows.
Bring in recordings in 10 audio and video formats, or re-transcribe an older meeting. Included in every edition.
Pro includes an MCP server, so Claude, Codex, Cursor or Windsurf can search meetings and read summaries. Off until you turn it on.
Weeks after the meeting, not only during it. Some of these use Pro integrations; see the workflow recipes.
Search old transcripts for the pricing discussion instead of scrolling through a month of notes.
Ask a connected assistant to list your action items from yesterday before standup.
Read the summary and the speaker-labeled transcript of the call you skipped.
A signed Pro webhook tells your own script a summary is ready, so it can post the notes to Slack or Notion.

children.text: You Decide What Leaves Your Computer

Recording and transcription run on your device, and the audio is never uploaded. Summaries use a local model, or your own API key for Claude, OpenAI or Groq if you prefer. A connected AI assistant sends what it reads to its own provider, so check how each provider handles data.
Whisper or Parakeet on your own hardware
Integrations wait until you switch them on

children.q: What is an AI meeting assistant?
children.a: An AI meeting assistant records and transcribes your calls, then helps with what comes after: a summary with decisions and action items, a record of past meetings you can search, and answers to questions like "what did we agree on last week?". Meetily transcribes on your own computer, and in Pro your AI assistant can work with your meeting history through MCP.

children.q: How is an AI meeting assistant different from an AI note taker?
children.a: A note taker writes up one meeting. An assistant also works across meetings: it finds the call where something was decided, lists open action items, and passes notes to the tools you already use. In Meetily, transcription and summaries are in every edition. Searching from an AI assistant or a script, and webhooks for automation, are Pro features.

children.q: Can I ask Claude about my past meetings?
children.a: Yes, with Meetily Pro. Pro includes an MCP server, and Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Windsurf connect in one click when they are installed on the same computer. The assistant can search your meetings and read transcripts and summaries. New connections start read-only, and starting or stopping a recording is a separate permission. Browser-based assistants such as Claude on the web cannot reach it. Keep in mind that an assistant sends what it reads to its own AI provider.

children.q: Does Meetily join my calls as a bot?
children.a: No. Meetily records the audio on your own computer, so no extra participant shows up in Zoom, Teams, Google Meet or any other app, and no host has to let anything in. As with any recorder, tell the people in the meeting that you are recording.

children.q: Can it send meeting notes to Slack, Notion or Jira?
children.a: Not with a built-in connector. Meetily Pro gives your own script a signed webhook when a summary is ready, and a command-line tool that exports any meeting as Markdown, text or JSON. The script then posts the notes wherever you want them. A connected AI assistant that already has access to those apps can do the same step for you.

Recording and transcription (Whisper or Parakeet) run on your computer, and the audio is never uploaded. Summaries use a local model through Ollama or the built-in model, or your own API key for Claude, OpenAI or Groq. With an API key, the transcript text goes to that provider under its terms. Zackriya Solutions does not receive your recordings or transcripts.

Yes. The Community Edition is free and open source (MIT license): live transcription, AI summaries, audio import and retranscription, all on your computer. Pro is $10/user/month billed annually and adds speaker diarization, custom summary templates, meeting detection with automatic recording, PDF and DOCX export, and the MCP server, CLI and webhooks. Pro comes with a 14-day trial.

children.q: Which platforms and languages does it support?
children.a: Meetily runs on Windows and on macOS with Apple Silicon. There is no native Linux app. It transcribes 99+ languages and works with any meeting app that plays audio on your computer, including Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Google Meet and Webex.
